summary: Nantucket Harbor Range Lights: two wooden skeletal towers on the Coast Guard grounds at Brant Point, placed in operation July 1908 to guide vessels into Nantucket Harbor.

light.characteristic: fixed white in 1908 (LH); current directory: quick-flashing white (front) and continuous white (rear)

structures.note: Located a few feet northeast of the old Brant Point Light (Rowlett).
81 m south-south-east of the front light, at the water's edge south of the old Brant Point Light (Rowlett).

access.note: Site and grounds open; towers closed. Coast Guard station grounds at the end of Easton Street (Rowlett; LH).

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (owner and site manager, per Rowlett)

events.note: Two wooden pyramidal skeletal range towers built on Brant Point (Rowlett; USLHS Brant Point record).
Placed in operation July 1908 when the Nantucket Cliff Range Lights were discontinued (LH).
Brant Point keeper Richard Dixon rescues two men from a motorboat that sank after ice damage; location relative to the range not stated.

keepers.name: Gerald M. Reed
keepers.note: Head keeper of Brant Point (LH keeper list gives 1927 to 1947; LH text gives 1926). The range lights appear only in his 1928 duty description, so this line records that year alone.

wrecks.outcome: Two men rescued by Brant Point keeper Richard Dixon after the boat was damaged by ice and sank. The source does not place the rescue relative to the range towers.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The USCG Historian's article 'Nantucket Range Lights' (history.uscg.mil, article 2008716) is the best official history, but neither the live page nor the archived copies could be read (HTTP 403). Read it before publication: it may settle the 1908 predecessor and the characteristics. Wikipedia (not cited) names the predecessor as the Nantucket Beacon and the Brant Point light; LH names the Cliff Range Lights. The record's 'range_nm 9.0' and 'QW' come from the USCG Light List, which was not read. The Lighthouse Friends keeper list headed 'Nantucket Harbor Beacon/Range' (1820-1880) covers the earlier beacon at the head of the harbour, not these towers, and is not used; the USLHS 'Nantucket Harbor Beacon' record is a different station. Reed's start year differs within LH (1926 in the text, 1927 in the keeper list). The 1928 duty description is quoted by LH without a primary citation; check the original before publication. The 1914 Bulletin lists a 'Nantucket Harbor, Mass., fixed to flashing' change without naming the light, so it is not used. The commissioner reports of 1918-1920 record an electric fog bell on the east breakwater, which is not the range and is not used. The Library of Congress record (2011630345) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Chronicling America was not searched for this station. Keepers are named only where a source ties them to the range; the towers have no roster of their own. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the directory's Cliff Range entry says 'Inactive since 1912' while LH says the Cliff Range lights were discontinued on 14 July 1908; both are stated in the story, not reconciled. The 1901 Board report's narrative (scan p. 81) says a new tower was built at the point and the light exhibited from it on 31 January 1901; the 'moved 596 feet' line (scan p. 31) is a single-line match, not a table column. The USLHS record lists the station as not open to the public, which the story gives alongside the directory's 'site open, tower closed'. The directory's 'Located at the ... Coast Guard Station, at the end of Easton Street' is in its 1856 Brant Point entry; the story uses it for the station's location.
